name: Careful Company: Chat & Webhook Egress
description: Blocks posting to outbound chat and webhook destinations: Slack incoming \ webhooks and Web API writes, Microsoft Teams connectors and Power Automate \ triggers, Discord webhooks, Telegram bot API, Google Chat spaces, Twilio \ messages, Zapier/IFTTT hooks, PagerDuty events, and request catchers such as \ webhook.site and interact.sh.

destructive_patterns.name: slack-incoming-webhook
destructive_patterns.description: Posting to a Slack incoming webhook sends data into a Slack channel.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
A `hooks.slack.com/services/...` URL accepts an unauthenticated POST and publishes the \ body into a channel. The URL is the credential, so anything that can read it can post \ — including whatever text or file contents the agent chose to include.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Print the message locally and let a person post it \ - Allowlist the exact command if a specific notification is approved

destructive_patterns.name: slack-web-api-write
destructive_patterns.description: Slack Web API write methods post messages or upload files to Slack.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`chat.postMessage` publishes a message and the `files.upload*` family uploads file \ content into a workspace, using a token already present on the machine. Read methods \ such as `conversations.history` are not affected by this rule.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use read-only Slack methods to look things up \ - Have a person post anything that needs to reach the workspace

destructive_patterns.name: teams-connector-webhook
destructive_patterns.description: Posting to a Microsoft Teams connector webhook sends data into a Teams channel.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
An Office 365 connector URL (`*.webhook.office.com/webhookb2/...`) accepts an \ unauthenticated POST and renders the payload as a card in a Teams channel. As with \ Slack, the URL itself is the only credential.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Leave the message on the console for a person to relay \ - Allowlist a specific, reviewed notification command

destructive_patterns.name: power-automate-trigger
destructive_patterns.description: Triggering a Power Automate / Logic Apps workflow URL sends the payload outside this machine.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Power Automate workflow URLs (`*.logic.azure.com/.../triggers/manual/paths/invoke`) are \ the replacement for retiring Office 365 connectors. The POST body is handed to a cloud \ workflow that can mail it, post it to Teams, or write it to storage.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Inspect the workflow definition rather than invoking it \ - Allowlist the specific trigger if this automation is approved

destructive_patterns.name: discord-webhook
destructive_patterns.description: Posting to a Discord webhook publishes data into a Discord channel.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
A Discord webhook URL accepts an unauthenticated POST with message content and file \ attachments, publishing them to a channel that is frequently outside company control.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Keep the output local and let a person share it \ - Allowlist the exact command if a specific bot notification is approved

destructive_patterns.name: telegram-bot-api
destructive_patterns.description: The Telegram bot API sends messages and documents to a chat.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage` and `/sendDocument` deliver text and files to \ any chat the bot can reach. The bot token in the URL is the whole authorization.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Keep the data local and have a person forward what is needed

destructive_patterns.name: google-chat-webhook
destructive_patterns.description: Posting to a Google Chat space webhook publishes data into that space.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`chat.googleapis.com/v1/spaces/<space>/messages?key=...` posts a message into a Google \ Chat space; the key and token in the query string are the only credential.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Print the message and let a person post it

destructive_patterns.name: twilio-message-send
destructive_patterns.description: The Twilio Messages API sends SMS or WhatsApp messages to arbitrary numbers.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
A POST to the Twilio `/Messages` resource sends an SMS or WhatsApp message using the \ account credentials on the machine — an outbound channel that leaves the corporate \ network entirely and reaches a personal device.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Read-only Twilio calls (usage, logs) are unaffected \ - Route approved messaging through the application, not an ad-hoc command

destructive_patterns.name: automation-platform-webhook
destructive_patterns.description: Zapier/IFTTT/PagerDuty event hooks forward the payload to a third-party automation.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
These endpoints hand the request body to an automation platform that can relay it \ onward — to mail, a spreadsheet, a chat channel, or an arbitrary HTTP call — under an \ account that may not be company-managed.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Inspect the automation instead of triggering it \ - Allowlist the specific trigger if it is an approved integration

destructive_patterns.name: request-catcher-service
destructive_patterns.description: Request-catcher services record whatever is sent to them.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
These services exist to capture and display arbitrary inbound requests, which makes them \ the default drop point for anything being taken off a machine. Payloads sit on a \ third-party server that anyone with the link can read. (Tunnel-rendezvous hostnames such \ as `*.ngrok.io` are owned by `tunnel:tunnel-client-binary`, whose keywords can actually \ reach them.)

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Point integration tests at a listener on localhost \ - Use a company-hosted endpoint for anything carrying real data

destructive_patterns.name: generic-incoming-webhook
destructive_patterns.description: A long opaque token under a /hooks/ path is an incoming-webhook endpoint.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Mattermost, Rocket.Chat, and many self-hosted chat servers publish incoming webhooks as \ `/hooks/<opaque-token>`. The shape is distinctive enough to flag, but generic enough \ that this rule warns rather than blocks — and an internally hosted chat server \ (loopback, RFC1918, `*.corp`/`*.internal`) is excluded outright.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - If this is your own chat server on a public address, allowlist the rule for that host \ - Otherwise treat the post as an outbound message and get it approved
